title: The AI Problem at Law Firms Isn't Hallucination. It's Honesty.
excerpt: Generic AI chatbots have a specific problem inside law firms: They answer honestly, even when the person asking isn't allowed to know the answer. Intapp's Ce...
content_html:
Some companies are built from a business plan. Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA) was founded in response to a complaint.

Back in the early 2000s, a small Silicon Valley outfit with a data integration product went to file a patent. The attorney handling the paperwork read the application and said that his law firm was a disaster in exactly this area. "Can I license this thing?" he asked.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Intapp said yes. The chief information officer at that law firm liked the product enough to quit his job, join Intapp as its first salesperson, and introduce the company to every law firm he knew. Referrals did the rest.

The company never raised venture capital, which is unusual for a Silicon Valley software business. Its first outside money arrived with the 2021 IPO. That history matters for reasons beyond color: Two decades of serving one narrow market produced the accumulated firm data and compliance infrastructure that management now calls Intapp's competitive moat.

A big market with an awkward shape

The company builds software for law firms, accounting firms, investment banks, private equity shops, and consultancies. CEO John Hall describes the customer base as "large partnership firms," a category he estimates at around $4 trillion in annual revenue in the United States. So it's a large market but also a tricky one to serve, and most software companies simply don't chase it.

Building the model is not the hard part. Knowing which of a firm's 3,000 employees may see which document, and proving it afterward, is. Large multipurpose AI vendors don't have the lived-in data set to copy Intapp's approach.

What "governed AI" actually means

Intapp launched its agentic AI platform, Celeste, at a February product event. It reached general availability on July 15. In a call with The Motley Fool, Hall outlined the distinction between Celeste and AI tools like Harvey (an Intapp partner) and Legora, which target the practice of law, as well as horizontal assistants like ChatGPT Enterprise.

The difference is permission. A generic AI assistant answers the question it is asked to the best of its automated ability.

"One of the problems with the horizontal systems is that they tell the truth," Hall said. "But you may not be a person who is supposed to get that answer inside the firm."

content_html_zh:
有些公司是根据商业计划建立的。 Intapp（纳斯达克股票代码：INTA）是为了回应投诉而成立的。

早在 2000 年代初，一家拥有数据集成产品的硅谷小型公司就申请了专利。 处理文书工作的律师阅读了申请表，并表示他的律师事务所在这方面就是一场灾难。 “我可以授权这个东西吗？” 他问道。

错过了 2009 年的 Nvidia？ 这个罕见的信号再次闪烁。 2009年，一家名不见经传的芯片制造商英伟达发出了“双倍下跌”的信号。 多年来，对于一家规模仅为 Nvidia 1/100 的公司来说，同样的“完全确信”信号闪烁。 继续 ”

因塔普说是的。 该律师事务所的首席信息官非常喜欢该产品，因此辞去了工作，加入 Intapp 作为第一位销售人员，并向他认识的每一家律师事务所介绍了该公司。 剩下的事情都是由推荐完成的。

该公司从未筹集过风险投资，这对于硅谷软件企业来说是不寻常的。 它的第一笔外部资金随着 2021 年 IPO 的到来而到来。 这段历史的重要性不仅仅体现在颜色上：二十年来服务于一个狭窄的市场，积累了公司数据和合规基础设施，管理层现在将其称为 Intapp 的竞争护城河。

形状尴尬的大市场

该公司为律师事务所、会计师事务所、投资银行、私募股权公司和咨询公司开发软件。 首席执行官约翰·霍尔 (John Hall) 将客户群描述为“大型合伙企业”，他估计这一类别在美国的年收入约为 4 万亿美元。 因此，这是一个很大的市场，但服务起来也很棘手，大多数软件公司根本不追逐这个市场。

构建模型并不是困难的部分。 了解公司 3,000 名员工中的哪些人可以看到哪份文档，并在事后证明这一点。 大型多用途人工智能供应商没有内置数据集来复制 Intapp 的方法。

“治理人工智能”的实际含义是什么

Intapp 在 2 月份的一次产品活动中推出了其代理人工智能平台 Celeste。 它于 7 月 15 日全面上市。 在与 The Motley Fool 的电话会议中，Hall 概述了 Celeste 与 Harvey（Intapp 合作伙伴）和 Legora 等人工智能工具（针对法律实践）以及 ChatGPT Enterprise 等横向助手之间的区别。

区别在于许可。 通用人工智能助手会尽其最大的自动化能力回答所提出的问题。

“水平系统的问题之一是它们说的是实话，”霍尔说。 “但你可能不是一个应该在公司内部得到答案的人。”
